bench.alt: Green plastic ruler held by binder clips at a glass table, with an orange wireless IMU secured at the free end.
bench.caption: The actual bench setup. A green plastic ruler is held at the table edge. Elastic bands secure an M5StickC Plus2 near its free end.

mount.alt: Close-up of the orange M5StickC Plus2 and the bands across the ruler.
mount.caption: Sensor attachment. This crop of the original photo shows why the board moves with the ruler and also adds mass.

clamp.alt: Close-up of the ruler crossing the glass table edge, held by clips.
clamp.caption: Clamp and free-length reference. This crop of the same photo shows the held end. In your own trial, measure from the effective clamp line to the tip.

ble-release-series.alt: The original BLE motion console with multiple bursts on its live graph.
ble-release-series.caption: Live motion console, first archived view. A release produces a burst and the trace settles before another release.

ble-live-trace.alt: The original BLE motion console displaying two ringdowns with a command panel and log.
ble-live-trace.caption: Live motion console, second archived view. The browser shows the changing signal next to controls and a log.

historic-model.alt: The archived spring-mass simulator with a spring drawing beside a fading oscillation.
historic-model.caption: Original Spring Mass Lab simulation capture. This explains the shape of a ringdown. It is not a recording of the ruler.

acceleration.alt: A measured acceleration waveform after release with successively smaller oscillations.
acceleration.caption: Measured run, acceleration-derived trace. The shrinking peaks show a ringdown after a release.

gyroscope.alt: A measured gyro x angular-rate trace showing the same ringdown.
gyroscope.caption: Measured run, gyro x. Rotational rate also oscillates and fades, using a different sensor channel.

spectrum.alt: Frequency spectrum of the acceleration-derived ringdown with a broad peak near 2.24 hertz.
spectrum.caption: Measured run, FFT. The main peak lies near 2.2 Hz. The width and coarse sampling matter more than the last decimal.

axis.alt: Principal-component variance plot, with almost all of the variance in the first component.
axis.caption: Measured run, PCA. Almost all acceleration variance in this window lies along one direction near the device z-axis. That identifies a direction at this sensor, not the full mode shape of the beam.
